title: The submerged plus maze as an assay for studying anxiety-like behaviour in fish
author: Hope, Hamilton, et al.

steps.title: Set up maze and video system
steps.instruction: Assemble the submerged plus‑maze apparatus, mount a video recorder directly above so the entire arena is visible, ensure uniform illumination with minimal glare, and position the experimenter out of the camera’s view.

steps.title: Fill maze with appropriate water
steps.instruction: Fill the maze to a depth of 10 cm with aerated stock‑tank water (or clean water from the fish habitat) whose temperature is 25 ± 1 °C and pH is 7–8, matching the fish’s home‑tank conditions.

steps.title: Prepare drug solution (if testing anxiolytics)
steps.instruction: Dissolve diazepam to a stock concentration of 100 mM in 0.5 % (v/v) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) prepared in aerated tank water; then dilute this stock with aerated tank water to a final volume of 500 mL to obtain a working concentration of 2.5 mg L⁻¹ (add 1.25 mg diazepam and 48.8 µL DMSO, then bring to 500 mL with water). Agitate gently to resuspend. Prepare a separate 500 mL holding container with aerated tank water for post‑immersion recovery.

steps.title: Transfer fish to drug exposure cup
steps.instruction: Using a dip net, gently lift the test fish from its home tank and place it into a slotted plastic cup (to minimise netting stress). Record the handling time.

steps.title: Drug immersion (optional)
steps.instruction: Immerse the cup containing the fish in the drug beaker for exactly 3 min (or the desired immersion time). The drug solution remains in the beaker; do not transfer it elsewhere.

steps.title: Post‑immersion recovery
steps.instruction: After the 3‑min immersion, lift the cup and place the fish into the prepared holding container for 5 min to allow the drug to take effect.

steps.title: Place fish in maze acclimation chamber
steps.instruction: Transfer the fish from the cup into the transparent acclimation cylinder (4.5 cm × 4.5 cm × 13 cm) that is positioned in the centre of the maze. Start the video recording at 1.5 min into the 2‑min acclimation period.

steps.title: Acclimation period
steps.instruction: Allow the fish to remain in the acclimation cylinder for a total of 2 min before release.

steps.title: Begin behavioural test
steps.instruction: Remove the acclimation cylinder, allowing the fish to explore the maze freely. Record behaviour for 5 min, avoiding any loud noises. Continue recording slightly beyond 5 min to capture the fish if water movement delays detection.

steps.title: Conclude test and return fish
steps.instruction: After the recording, gently return the fish to its home tank.

steps.title: Arena maintenance between trials
steps.instruction: If possible, replace the maze water between fish; otherwise keep the water temperature, pH and other parameters stable and aerated. If temperature drops by ~3 °C or chemistry changes markedly, replace or adjust the water. Rotate the maze after each trial to eliminate spatial or visual biases.

steps.title: Score behaviour (automated)
steps.instruction: Analyse the video with automated tracking software (e.g., EthoVision). Ensure lighting does not cause glare and that the fish contrasts with the background.

steps.title: Score behaviour (manual, if needed)
steps.instruction: Manually note the time of each arm entry and count how many 1.5 cm lines the fish crosses within each arm.

steps.title: Calculate behavioural metrics
steps.instruction: Sum the total time spent and the number of line crossings in each of the three zones: visually closed arms, visually open arms, and centre area. Count the number of entries into new arms and specifically into visually open arms.

description: This apparatus was validated using the anxiety-reducing (anxiolytic) benzodiazepine diazepam administered by immersion (Fig. 3) [[12], [13], [14], [15]]. Immersion is the method of choice because injection of substances requires anesthesia with MS-222 or cold water, which can impair behavioural responses. Immersion can quickly and reliably be used to validate anxiety-like behavioural tests with other anxiolytic substances (e.g., ethanol) [16], as well as anxiogenic substances (e.g., GABAA receptor antagonist, gabazine) [17,18]. Note that time of immersion in a drug solution can vary from 3 min (e.g., Diazepam) [12,15] up to thirty minutes [16]. If a longer duration of immersion is used, the dosing beaker should be kept under a heating mat to maintain water temperature [16]. To reduce the amount of handling the fish experienced, we used a slotted plastic cup to transport fish between each step. This likely minimizes netting stress and damage to the slime coat of the fish. Fish were housed individually in aquaria partitioned by transparent dividers to control for aggression and social isolation effects and to ensure handling stress was restricted to the fish of interest.1Dissolve diazepam (100 mM) in a 0.5% solution of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) in aerated tank water.
